quick_reference.text: Name the actor or object and use a concrete verb, such as participants provided, the analysis found, or the method infers.
Use binary evaluative feedback, scalar evaluative feedback, and *progress* consistently. Keep human annotations distinct from learned rewards and policies, and keep the definitions Hang wrote.
Describe progress through the degree of task completion. Keep scale endpoints tied to the particular study and definition.

Report observations directly, interpretations with appropriate qualification, and untested explanations as possibilities. Keep the reporting frame of a result, such as Results indicate that. Hang writes both which suggests that and suggesting that.
Give the measure, baseline, condition, and relevant uncertainty together. No significant difference was detected does not mean the two conditions are equivalent.
patterns: Reporting a difference that was not detected

quick_reference.text: Qualify a result when the sentence misstates the evidence, such as a no-difference claim, an unmeasured intention, or a guarantee. Ask before removing significantly from a result the chapter tests, or adding a caveat sentence.
Describe imperfect signals and actions precisely. Explain human or interface constraints without attributing unmeasured motives or blame.

Give each sentence one main job and keep a governing condition attached. Split two findings or two studies into two sentences. Keep together a result and the which clause that interprets it, a chain joined by but, and a numbered list of questions or findings.
patterns: One main job and varied sentence length

quick_reference.text: Define the signal or quantity before formal notation. Explain the intuition before the method's operations and evaluation.
patterns: An intuition leading to an operation

quick_reference.text: Open a research chapter with its stage sentence and then its own introduction, from the gap to the findings, ending with the related work and the published version. Keep This chapter as the subject of argues, asks, analyzes, defines, measures, and builds on.
Connect chapters through questions and contributions while preserving differences in tasks, participants, scales, and evaluations. Name the stages modeling, mitigating, and leveraging.

Use few colons and semicolons. State the relation in words with which, since, because, such as, or whereas, or start a new sentence. Keep a colon before a numbered list, after The key intuition is that, before the clause that spells out a named property, and before a quotation. Replace em dashes.
Write complete clauses. Give a comparison its own subject and verb instead of ending on did, does not, or so.
patterns: Complete clauses in place of elliptical endings

entries.title: Few colons and semicolons
entries.guidance: Use few colons and semicolons. Hang stated this preference on October 12, 2026, after the Chapter 8 review, and it takes priority over the punctuation of the papers and of earlier drafts. Before writing either mark, try to state the relation in words. A relative clause (which is to, which are) can introduce what a colon would introduce. Since or because can attach a reason, and such as or including can attach examples. Whereas, while, or but can carry a contrast that a semicolon would carry, and a second statement can be a new sentence. A colon remains suitable when a complete lead-in announces a list of several items or a term. Semicolons remain suitable between the items of a long list whose items contain commas.
forms: [Design choice] recurs in [chapters], which is to [operation].
[Claim], since [reason].
[Statement about A], whereas [statement about B].
[General statement], for instance, [case].
[Statement]. [Second statement].
[Strategy] would be compared with several [baselines]: [item A, with detail]; [item B]; and [item C].
entries.boundary: This is a preference for fewer marks, not a ban, and the punctuation review of October 12, 2026 showed where the line is. Hang kept a colon in four places. The first is before a numbered or listed set of questions, findings, premises, or alternatives, such as Each stage addresses one question: whether ... The second is after The key intuition is that, before the emphasized statement of the intuition. The third is after a sentence that names a property, such as is operational or suggests the underlying reasons, before the clause that spells it out. The fourth is before a quotation. Hang accepted removing a colon after a verb or a preposition, such as are and between, joining a short list to its sentence with such as, including, namely, or by, and splitting two complete statements at a colon or semicolon, as in a chapter roadmap. Hang also accepted replacing every em dash that was reviewed, with a comma, a which clause, or a new sentence. Do not put a dash or a pair of parentheses where the colon or semicolon was, since the sentence would keep the same break. Do not join two statements with and when their relation is a reason or a contrast. Name the relation. Punctuation inside equations, citations, headings, LaTeX commands, and quoted source text is outside this preference.

entries.title: A motivation told as a story
entries.guidance: Tell the motivation of a talk or a film as a short story about the problem, in the order of Hang's outline. Robots are already part of daily life, but most training data are recorded in labs, and many learning methods require clean data. For robots to be part of everyday life, they need to learn from everyone. Not everyone can provide clean data, and people teach each other through many modalities. Non-expert teaching is also more accessible, and models trained on it can be more robust in the real world. Set up the problem rather than summarizing what the dissertation already did, and do not overstate what robots can do now.
forms: Most of the data that robots learn from is recorded in labs, by experts and trained operators.
Many learning methods require clean data.
For robots to become part of our everyday lives, they need to learn from everyone, including people who have never used a robot.
However, not everyone can provide clean data.
When people teach people, they do more than talk.
Non-expert teaching, while noisy, is the teaching that robots will receive from the people they live and work with.
entries.boundary: Hang rejected a draft of the film for being too specific about the dissertation's own work, and called the first motivation slides too serious, too wordy, and not illustrative. Hang asked for the outline to be followed in idea, not word for word. Each caption should say its point plainly. A noise label that appears before the scene shows why, and a reference that the audience has to decode, such as the name of a painting or a quotation from an 1874 review, were rejected or removed. The motivation slides follow benefits, then the challenge, then this work.
